ledger.claim: POL-NS-23 makes the driver's pre-cancellation contact obligation conjunctive: before cancelling for no-show the driver must have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call. The trip record's own derived contact check reports message_count 0 and obligation_met false, so the message limb fails outright and the 5.00 SGD fee must be voided with a FULL_REFUND of the fee charged and no driver compensation.

The chat log for this trip carries exactly one entry, and it is the rider's own message 'Coming down now, sorry', sent at 12:21:50 and delivered at 12:21:53 — forty seconds AFTER the driver cancelled at 12:21:10. There is no driver message at any point in the log, before or after the cancellation, so nothing in the record can satisfy the message limb of POL-NS-23.

The driver's own account is 'I called two times, no answer.' That asserts calls and nothing else: it does not claim, and the record nowhere shows, that any in-app message was ever sent to the rider. The two in-app calls at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40 (unanswered, 20 s and 18 s) establish the call limb of POL-NS-23 and only the call limb.

The rider's admission that his phone was on silent explains only why the two calls rang out; it does not touch the separate requirement that the driver also message him in the app. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive — a ringing call is not a message — and on this record the rider was left with no in-app notice of where the driver was waiting or that he was about to be cancelled on.

The rider sent 'Coming down now, sorry' forty seconds after the driver cancelled, which shows he was responding and on his way down rather than lost to the trip. A single in-app message from the driver, which POL-NS-23 requires and which costs nothing, would have reached him before the cancellation instead of after it.

Candidly, the arrival and wait prerequisites are met on this record: auto-arrival at 12:15:30 is corroborated by the GPS trace (nearest fix 3.07 m from the pickup point at 6 m reported accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius), and cancellation at 12:21:10 is 340 s after arrival — past the 300 s free wait. The fee therefore stands or falls on the contact obligation in POL-NS-23 alone, and there it falls.

Every fact POL-NS-23 needs is carried by COMPLETE evidence at weight 1.0 — the trip record and the chat log — so POL-GEN-26 is not engaged and no question is left open for a human. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and no fraud flag is recorded on either profile, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on this no-show is final and the refund issues without escalation.

The payments ledger records exactly 5.00 SGD charged as the cancellation fee, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the ledger's own money block puts refund_if_voided_sgd at 5.00. The remedy the record supports is therefore FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD — the whole contested amount returned — with no driver compensation, which is precisely what POL-NS-23 prescribes when the contact obligation is unmet.

No repeat no-show referral arises under POL-NS-25: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter at all, and the fee cannot stand, so this trip cannot be counted toward the threshold of 3. There is nothing on this record to flag the rider's account for review.

The driver was at the pickup when arrival was logged: on the GPS trace the nearest fix to the pickup point is 3.07 m away with a reported accuracy of 6 m, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius that POL-NS-21 sets, and the trace's own arrival check records corroborated = true. The arrival event at 12:15:30 is therefore made out on the trip record and corroborated by the trace.

The trip is on-demand and carries no scheduled pickup time, so under POL-NS-21 the 300 s free wait runs from the driver's arrival at 12:15:30 and expired at 12:20:30. The driver cancelled at 12:21:10 - 340 s after arrival and 40 s after the wait expired - so the free-wait condition for cancelling as a rider no-show is satisfied.

The amount charged is the policy amount: the payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD with fee_matches_policy = true, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, matching POL-NS-22's 5.00 SGD no-show fee. Where the fee stands, POL-NS-22 makes the ruling DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00.

The call limb of the driver's contact obligation is satisfied: the trip record's in-app call log shows two calls the driver placed to the rider before cancellation, at 12:17:55 (rang 20 s) and 12:19:40 (rang 18 s), neither answered, and the rider's own claim concedes the calls ('He did call').

The rider was not at the pickup, so the no-show is factual and not merely asserted: the platform pushed 'Your driver has arrived' to the rider at 12:15:34 with live tracking enabled, and the rider's only in-app message, 'Coming down now, sorry', was sent at 12:21:50 - 40 s after the driver cancelled at 12:21:10 - showing the rider was still on the way down when the driver gave up after the full wait.

The driver's advocate does not assert, and this record does not show, any in-app chat message sent by the driver before cancellation: EV-CHAT-05053 carries a single entry and it is the rider's, and trip_record.chat_message_count is 1, so the message limb of POL-NS-23 is not made out on the present evidence. The driver's case therefore rests on the completed free wait, the corroborated arrival and the two call attempts, and it is for the Judge to weigh the contact obligation on that record.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged on TRP-05053 is voided and refunded in full.

The arrival and wait steps were done properly. Auto-arrival at the pickup is logged at 12:15:30, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-05053) corroborates it — the nearest fix is 3.07 m from the pickup point with a reported accuracy of 6 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets; the trip record's own arrival check records corroborated = true. Because this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled pickup time, POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from arrival (12:15:30), so it expired at 12:20:30; the driver cancelled at 12:21:10, 340 s after arrival and 40 s after the wait expired. The POL-NS-21 prerequisites are therefore met, and I accept the driver's submissions to that effect.

The fee nevertheless falls on POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3), the driver's contact obligation, which requires that before cancelling for no-show the driver have sent at least one in-app chat message to the rider AND placed at least one in-app call, both before trip_record.cancelled_at. Only the call limb is met: the trip record's in-app call log shows two calls placed by the driver at 12:17:55 and 12:19:40 (unanswered, 20 s and 18 s), which the rider concedes ('He did call'). The message limb is not met on any view. EV-CHAT-05053 carries exactly one message and it is the rider's own ('Coming down now, sorry'), sent at 12:21:50 — forty seconds after the driver cancelled at 12:21:10 — and the trip record's derived contact check records message_count 0 and obligation_met false. No in-app message was ever sent by the driver, before or after cancellation, and the driver's own account ('I called two times, no answer') asserts calls and nothing else. POL-NS-23 is conjunctive — a ringing call is not a message — so the missing message voids the fee: FULL_REFUND of the fee charged, with no driver compensation. EV-FARE-05053 shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and its money block puts refund_if_voided_sgd at 5.00, so the sum returned is 5.00 SGD.

On the driver's remaining submissions: the arrival, free-wait and fee-amount points are correct and accepted, but they do not save the fee, because POL-NS-23 is an independent precondition that the record shows was not satisfied; the driver's advocate itself recorded that the message limb is not made out. On the rider's submissions: the conjunctive reading of POL-NS-23 is correct, the chat log shows no driver message before cancellation, and the whole contested amount is returned with no driver compensation.

No referral arises. POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire: the amount charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so the fee-amount referral for a non-standard amount is not triggered. POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not fire: the driver did arrive at the pickup and did attempt contact, so the clause's condition is not met. POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not fire: rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is absent from the profile, and the fee does not stand, so this trip cannot be counted toward the threshold of 3.

On the decision route: the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, no fraud flag is recorded on either profile, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final. POL-GEN-26 is not engaged, because every fact POL-NS-23 needs is carried by COMPLETE evidence at weight 1.0 — EV-TRIP-05053 and EV-CHAT-05053 — and no question is left open for a human reviewer.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
